review_notes: I read the whole file and the related ScalarExtension.lean, Dual.lean and K0.lean (for hom_ext_ofClass and lift_ofClass). I grepped for existing ring-equivalence-induced additive equivalences on ProjectiveClass and found none, so a `mapEquiv` would be new API. I also checked for shared K₀ localization-transport lemmas and found none; the idiom is inlined in ScalarExtension.lean, in Dual.lean, and twice in this file. Short rfl wrappers and the symmetric fst/snd module-equivalence blocks in `prodEquiv_symm_of_module` were left out. They are asymmetric, and a helper there would mostly move duplicated branches. I did not compile the proposed lemmas, so the statements and proof sketches may need small adjustments such as universe or instance details.

findings.problem: Both bijectivity proofs repeat the same argument: transport a K₀-localization map along a class-level additive equivalence, then compare with the target homomorphism on generators. Each one proves the `htop` surjectivity fact by hand and builds `qA := q.ofAddEquivOfDom ... htop`. Each then takes `AddLocalization.addEquivOfQuotient qA`, proves `hforward` with `hom_ext_ofClass`, `addEquivOfQuotient_addMonoidOf` and `map_ofClass`, and finishes with `rw [← hforward]; exact e.bijective`. The prod version is at lines 679–709. ScalarExtension.lean's `map_bijective_of_projectiveClass_map_bijective` does the same with `addEquivOfAddEquiv`, so the pattern appears three times. Only the localization map `qPi` or `qRS` and the generator computation differ.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma (in ScalarExtension.lean or here). Statement: for `e : ProjectiveClass A ≃+ P` with `P` an `AddCommMonoid`, `G` an `AddCommGroup`, `q : AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap (⊤ : AddSubmonoid P) G`, `f : K0 A →+ G`, and `hf : ∀ a, f (ofClass A a) = q (e a)`, conclude `Function.Bijective f`. Proof sketch: `htop` from `e.symm`; `qA := q.ofAddEquivOfDom (k := e) htop`; `E := AddLocalization.addEquivOfQuotient qA`; `E.toAddMonoidHom = f` by `hom_ext_ofClass` plus `addEquivOfQuotient_addMonoidOf` plus `hf`; then `E.bijective`. Rewritten uses: in `K0.piEquiv`, `exact K0.bijective_of_localizationMap (ProjectiveClass.piEquiv Ri) qPi (piMap Ri) (fun a => funext fun i => map_ofClass (Pi.evalRingHom Ri i) a)`. In `K0.prodEquiv`, the same with `ProjectiveClass.prodEquiv R S`, `qRS` and `(map fst).prod (map snd)`, using `Prod.ext (map_ofClass _ a) (map_ofClass _ a)` for `hf`. Both uses keep their current hypotheses (`Finite ι` for pi, and arbitrary rings for prod) and the same imports. Only the construction of `qPi` and `qRS` stays inline.
findings.benefit: This removes about 30 duplicated lines per use and gives one audited place for the transport argument. Each equivalence is then reduced to what is specific to it: the product localization map and the generator formula. The ScalarExtension lemma could be restated through the same helper.

findings.problem: The proof hand-builds three additive equivalences `eA`, `eR` and `eS` from ring equivalences `q`, `dR` and `dS`. Each is the same structure: `toFun := map e`, `invFun := map e.symm`, `left_inv` and `right_inv` by `map_comp`, `RingEquiv.*_toRingHom_comp_*` and `map_id`, and `map_add'`. That is six copies of the same functoriality argument, with only the ring equivalence changing. The `hforward` proof then repeats a three-step `map_comp` calculation for fst and for snd (lines 272–291), differing only in the projection used.
findings.proposed_change: Add a general definition near `ProjectiveClass.map_comp` and `map_id` in ScalarExtension.lean. Statement: `ProjectiveClass.mapEquiv (e : R ≃+* S) : ProjectiveClass R ≃+ ProjectiveClass S` with `toFun := map e.toRingHom` and `invFun := map e.symm.toRingHom`. The inverse laws are the four-line `map_comp`/`map_id` argument currently inlined. Also add `mapEquiv_apply : mapEquiv e a = map e.toRingHom a`. In `prodEquiv`, replace `eA`, `eR` and `eS` by `mapEquiv q.symm`, `mapEquiv dR` and `mapEquiv dS`. For `hforward`, rewrite each component as `rw [← map_comp_apply, ← map_comp_apply]` or `simp only [← map_comp_apply]` followed by `rw [hfst]`, which collapses the two calc blocks. This needs no extra imports. It works for arbitrary rings, including zero rings, since only functoriality is used.
findings.benefit: The proof shortens by roughly 40 lines. The ring-equivalence-to-class-equivalence step becomes reusable API; other files already build additive equivalences from ring equivalences ad hoc. `prodEquiv` then reads as a composite of named equivalences.

findings.problem: The same module-level fact is proved three times, each time by spelling out the same `of_eq_of_equiv` linear equivalence `mapLinearEquiv (piLinearEquiv Ri Mi)` composed with `piRecoverLinearEquiv`. Coordinate `i` of the scalar extension of the product module is isomorphic to `Mi i`. The copies are in the surjectivity half of `ProjectiveClass.piEquiv` (lines 97–104), in `ProjectiveClass.piEquiv_symm_of_module` (lines 152–156), and in `K0.piEquiv_symm_of_module` (lines 560–566). Each wraps the fact in a different context.
findings.proposed_change: State once, before `piEquiv`: `theorem ProjectiveClass.map_evalRingHom_of_pi (Mi : ∀ i, ModuleCat.FiniteProjective.{uR, uM} (Ri i)ᵐᵒᵖ) (i : ι) [Finite ι] : map (Pi.evalRingHom Ri i) (of (∀ j, Ri j) (ModuleCat.FiniteProjective.pi Ri Mi)) = of (Ri i) (Mi i)`. The proof is `rw [map_of]; exact of_eq_of_equiv (Ri i) _ ((mapLinearEquiv ...).trans (piRecoverLinearEquiv ...))`. Then the surjectivity branch is `⟨of _ (pi Ri Mi), funext fun i => (this.trans (hMi i))⟩`. `ProjectiveClass.piEquiv_symm_of_module` becomes `(piEquiv Ri).injective (funext fun i => (this ..).symm)` after `apply_symm_apply`. `K0.piEquiv_symm_of_module` can use `simpa [piEquiv_apply, K0.map_of, ofClass_of]` with the lemma's `of` form, or the existing `rw [piEquiv_of_module]` followed by `congrArg (ofClass _)` of the class lemma. The statement holds with `uM = uR` in the surjectivity use. The `Finite ι` variable is only needed for the equivalence-based applications.
findings.benefit: The linear-equivalence recipe, which is the only nontrivial mathematics in these proofs, is written and maintained once instead of three times. The three consumers shrink to a few lines each. A change to the recovery equivalence or its universe annotations no longer has to be repeated by hand.
